prompt: A patient weighs $154\text{ lb}$. Medication orders on this unit are written per kilogram of body weight. Using $1\text{ kg}=2.2\text{ lb}$, what is the patient's mass in kilograms?
teacher_notes: Students who multiply instead of divide will report 338.8 kg, which is a useful reasonableness check to discuss.
explanation: Divide the weight in pounds by the conversion factor: $\frac{154\text{ lb}}{2.2\text{ lb/kg}}=70\text{ kg}$. Converting before calculating a weight-based dose is a routine patient safety step.
